title: Add syntax highlighting with syntect behind a cargo feature
description: Cargo feature 'syntax', on by default, with syntect (default-features off, regex-fancy, default-syntaxes) and two-face for TypeScript, TSX, TOML and more. No C code. syntect only splits lines into scopes, and a scope-to-role table in the theme gives the colours, so highlighting follows the flavor. Highlight against the whole file: the new side from the work tree, the old side from 'git show <rev>:path' through the git parameter, tokenised when the file comes on screen and cached. Files over about 1 MiB, and files that cannot be read, fall back to each hunk as a snippet, and an unknown language draws plain. Highlight colours replace the text colour and the add/remove tint stays behind them. Build with --no-default-features must still pass.
acceptance_criteria: Tests cover scope-to-role mapping, a multi-line block comment and template string coloured correctly from the whole file, the hunk-snippet fallback, an unknown extension, the old side of a renamed file, the cache, and cargo build/test/clippy with and without the feature. stage-local.sh builds with the feature. Binary size and cold build time are recorded in the close note.

title: Draw applied comments as rounded boxes like hunk's Your note
description: An open thread is a rounded full-width box. The top border reads '● <author> · <relative time> · <path> R<line>' (author is 'Your note' for the user, the agent's name otherwise), then the badges [outdated], [new], (edited since sent) and an unsent mark. The path is cut from the left with an ellipsis, side letter R or L. The body is wrapped inside, replies follow indented. The bottom border carries the keys, read from the keymap: 'R reply  E edit  D delete' for the user's comments, only 'R reply' for an agent's. A resolved thread stays one line with a green check in place of the bullet. Comment gets the event's 'at' timestamp from the fold so the card can show 'now', '2m', '3h', '2d'. The label is computed when the stream is built, with no timer.
acceptance_criteria: Tests cover the user and agent boxes, badges, replies, the resolved one-liner, the footer keys following a rebound keymap, the relative-time labels from fixed timestamps, path cutting, both layouts, and that card rows still map to comments for focused_comment. Existing card tests are updated, not deleted.

title: Draw the comment editor as a rounded box like hunk's Draft note
description: The editor is a rounded border in the theme's warning (yellow) colour, the full width of the stream in both layouts, under the commented row or above it when there is no room. The title is ' Draft note - <path> R<line> ' (L for the old side, R101-110 for a range, just the path for a file comment), cut from the left with an ellipsis when long. The bottom border carries '^S save  Esc cancel' on the right, or the save error. While the editor is empty it shows a dim 'Write a note…'. The commented row (or range) keeps a bright left bar and tint while the editor is open. Reply and edit use the same box with 'Reply to <id>' and 'Edit <id>' titles.
acceptance_criteria: TestBackend tests cover the box in unified and side-by-side, the title for line, range, old side and file, the placeholder, the footer and a failed-save footer, the highlighted target row, and the height cap. editor_rect no longer indents by GUTTER.

title: Add a Catppuccin theme and route every colour through it
description: One Theme struct of named colour roles (base, text, subtle text, border, accent, cursor, selection, added and removed tints, header bar, sidebar, prompts, syntax scopes). Four flavors as constant tables: catppuccin-mocha (default), -macchiato, -frappe, -latte. Chosen with [theme] name = "..." in the plugin's config.toml, read once at start next to [keys]. An unknown name warns through Warning::Config and falls back to mocha. Every hard-coded Color:: in src/ (view.rs, cards.rs, editor.rs, tui.rs) moves to a role. The pane paints the theme's base colour as its background, truecolor only.
acceptance_criteria: No Color:: outside the theme module. Tests cover each flavor loading, the unknown-name warning, an invalid [theme] table, and a rendered buffer showing the base background and a tint taken from the theme. PLAN.md 7.1 documents the [theme] table.
close_reason: theme.rs holds one Theme of colour roles and four Catppuccin flavors as constant tables. [theme] name in config.toml picks one, read once in App::new beside the keymap. An unknown name, a name that is not a string and a theme that is not a table each warn through Warning::Config and fall back to mocha. No Color:: is left outside theme.rs. The DIM modifier became the theme's subtle text colour. render paints the base and text colour on every cell still on the terminal's colours. Tints are the flavor's green and red mixed 15 percent into its base. PLAN.md 7.1, 12.1, 12.2 and the TUI start graph document it. Syntax roles are left for the syntax bead, where they are used.

title: Add a side-by-side diff that follows the width
description: At 120 columns or more the diff draws old on the left and new on the right, below that it stays unified. A remappable key, default t, forces the other layout until pressed again or restart. A run of removed lines pairs row by row with the added run after it. Rows are tinted red and green, with line numbers in both gutters. A '▾ N unchanged lines' row sits above the first hunk and between hunks, computed from the gaps, display only. Each file starts with a header: path on the left, +N -N on the right, a rule between files. Comment cards span the full width under their row. c and v use the new half, or the old half on a removed-only row, and a click uses the half under the mouse. Rows stop being one unified diff line each, so Stream, locate, offset_of, capture and the mouse handler change.
acceptance_criteria: TestBackend tests cover both layouts at their widths, the toggle key, pairing, unchanged-lines rows, cards in both layouts, and comment capture on each side. Range selection stays inside one file and one side. The existing unified tests still pass.
close_reason: At 120 columns or more the diff draws side by side, below that unified. The t key (toggle_layout, remappable) forces the other layout. Removed runs pair with the added run after them, rows are tinted, line numbers show on both halves, file headers carry +N -N, and unchanged-lines rows mark the gaps. Cards stay full width. c and v use the new half, or the old half of a removed-only row, and a click picks the half. Deviation: the unchanged-lines rows appear only in the side-by-side layout, so unified keeps the diff's rows and its existing tests. The file header uses a tinted bar in place of a rule between files. PLAN.md 7 has a 'How the layout behaves' block.

title: Build the CLI edge and 'comment list'
description: In main.rs, parse arguments into a Command enum, read Env once, resolve the repo root, and map every error to stderr and an exit code as in PLAN.md section 12.6. Implement 'comment list' with its filters and --json. Below main.rs, functions receive git, herdr, dir, now and env as parameters (section 12.3).
acceptance_criteria:
- No std::env or Command::new call exists outside main.rs, herdr.rs and the git runner.
- Exit codes follow section 12.6: usage errors give 2, a non-repo directory gives 1.
- 'comment list --json' output parses back into the same threads.
close_reason: CLI edge and 'comment list' done. main.rs reads the process once into Env; open, spike-send and tui take it. The git runner starts diff.rs. PLAN.md section 2 lists cli.rs, comment.rs and env.rs.

title: Implement 'comment reply', 'resolve' and 'reopen'
description: Implement the three subcommands from PLAN.md section 5 on top of store::write. Text comes from stdin only. An agent resolve must carry a reply (ADR 0004).
acceptance_criteria:
- A wrong id exits 2 and prints the open ids.
- 'resolve' without --reply exits 2.
- A second 'resolve' or 'reopen' exits 0 and writes nothing.
- A reply text containing backticks and $(...) is stored byte for byte.
close_reason: reply, resolve and reopen done. PLAN.md 12.1 now lists InvalidBody for bad reply text and drops NotAllowed, which no comment subcommand can raise. The agent name comes from --name only until apply adds detection.

title: Implement meta.json load and save
description: Implement Meta as described in PLAN.md sections 3.1 and 12.5, including the scan of sibling directories by root when the hashed directory name does not match.
acceptance_criteria:
- A save changes only the caller's fields and keeps the rest.
- An unreadable meta.json loads as an empty Meta with a MetaUnreadable warning.
- Two processes saving different fields at once both keep their change.
close_reason: meta.json load, locked save and sibling scan done in src/meta.rs. PLAN.md section 2 lists the new file.

title: Define the shapes and the fold
description: In store.rs, define the ids, Event, Author, Comment, Thread, Anchor, Status and Review from PLAN.md section 12.1, with serde for the JSONL form in section 3.2. Write fold(events) -> Review following the fold rules in section 3.2 and the rights in ADR 0004. This task is pure: no file access.
acceptance_criteria:
- Ids are newtypes that only their parser can build.
- One unit test per fold rule in PLAN.md section 3.2, plus: unknown id skipped, an agent editing a user comment skipped, deleting a root removes the thread, edit after sent sets edited_since_sent and leaves the thread sent.
close_reason: Fold and shapes done. PLAN.md 3.2 now says an agent-written root is not unsent by itself, which section 6.1 already assumed.

title: Implement store::write and the tolerant reader
description: Implement the graph 'Write to the store' in PLAN.md section 12.4 and the reader in section 3.4, with the state directory from section 3.1. Use std::fs::File locking (ADR 0002). The reader also supports reading from a byte offset for the TUI.
acceptance_criteria:
- Every E: line of the graph has a test.
- 8 processes appending 200 events each leave 1600 valid lines and no duplicate id.
- A file truncated mid-line still yields every earlier event and one SkippedLine warning.
- A lock held by another process gives Busy after about 2 seconds. Killing the holder frees the lock.
- A build closure that returns an error leaves the file unchanged.
close_reason: Store write, tolerant reader and state dir done. Lock poll changed from 50 ms to 2 ms plus a 2 ms pause on release, because 8 looping writers starved a 50 ms poller into Busy. PLAN.md 3.3 and 12.4 updated.

title: Spike: prompt delivered to a working Claude Code
description:
## Goal

Use 'spike-send' while Claude Code is mid-turn (W13 in RESEARCH.review.md). Observe when the prompt is handled, and what happens to it when the user presses Esc before it is handled. ADR 0003 depends on the answer.

## Findings

Fill in when the spike is done: what was run, what was observed, and what it changes.
acceptance_criteria:
- docs/adr/0003 'Consequences' states the observed behaviour for both cases.
- If a queued prompt can be lost, a follow-up bead exists for how send should report it.
close_reason: Working agent queues the prompt and answers it as the next turn; Esc interrupts the running turn and the queued prompt is then submitted, not lost. ADR 0003 updated. No follow-up needed.

title: Spike: pane id stability, decide ADR 0006
description:
## Goal

Find out when a public pane id changes and whether terminal_id survives. Try: closing a sibling pane, moving the pane to another tab, moving it to another workspace, restarting the Herdr server with session restore. Compare 'herdr pane list' before and after, and the HERDR_PANE_ID seen by a process already running in the pane.

## Findings

Fill in when the spike is done: what was run, what was observed, and what it changes.
acceptance_criteria:
- docs/adr/0006 has status accepted or rejected, with the observed cases listed.
- If rejected, PLAN.md section 6.2 is rewritten to match and the beads that cite ADR 0006 are updated.
close_reason: ADR 0006 accepted with the observed cases. Terminal id survives moves but not a server restart, noted in PLAN.md 6.2. Not rejected, so no rewrite of 6.2 or other beads.

title: Spike: environment, action context and keys
description:
## Goal

Answer three questions on the installed Herdr and write each answer into PLAN.md section 11. (1) Do REVIEW_DELIVER_TO and REVIEW_DELIVER_TERM passed with --env reach the pane process (W15)? (2) Is an action with contexts = ["pane"] offered and runnable while the review pane is focused, and what does focused_pane_id hold then (W24)? (3) Do prefix+i and prefix+shift+i bind as plugin_action without a duplicate-key warning?

## Findings

Fill in when the spike is done: what was run, what was observed, and what it changes.
acceptance_criteria:
- PLAN.md section 11 states each answer with the command that showed it.
- An answer that contradicts the plan has a follow-up bead linked with discovered-from.
close_reason: All three answered in PLAN.md section 11; none contradicts the plan, so no follow-up bead. The pane-offered half of the action-context question can only be checked by hand with a bound key.

title: Create the Cargo project, manifest and stage script
description: Create the crate at the repository root with the layout in PLAN.md section 2 and the manifest in section 8. Add hunk/, zeron/ and herdr-annotate/ to .gitignore, they are reference clones. Copy lints and the release profile from herdr-annotate/rust/Cargo.toml. For now the 'open' action opens the 'tui' pane with the flags in PLAN.md section 5 'open' step 4, using the focused pane as the agent pane, and the pane prints its environment and HERDR_PLUGIN_CONTEXT_JSON, then waits for a key.
acceptance_criteria:
- scripts/stage-local.sh builds and places bin/herdr-review.
- 'herdr plugin link .' succeeds and 'herdr plugin action list --plugin review' shows open and send.
- Invoking the open action from an agent pane opens a split to its right that prints the variables.
- cargo clippy and cargo test are clean.
close_reason: Crate, manifest and stage script in place; link lists open and send; open split prints the variables

title: Copy the reusable modules from herdr-annotate
description: Copy herdr.rs, agent_delivery.rs, termination.rs, edit_keys.rs and width.rs from herdr-annotate/rust/src/ with exactly the changes in PLAN.md section 2.1. Add a hidden 'spike-send' action that calls deliver_to_agent(Delivery::Send, ...) with a fixed two-line prompt to the focused pane.
acceptance_criteria:
- The copied tests that remain pass.
- No copied file imports a module that does not exist in this crate.
- 'spike-send' against an idle Claude Code pane starts a turn.
close_reason: Copied modules build and their tests pass; spike-send to an idle Claude Code started a turn (reply: received)
